brief: Futures slide pre-market, tech-led, as a tanker strike off Qatar pushes Brent to $105 and WTI near $92, lifting the 10-year to 5.33% and the dollar while Bitcoin falls with risk appetite; GS flags that Hormuz-area risk can spread, and notes sovereign-risk concern is spreading from France into Italy and Greece. Industrials cyclicals (CAT, HUBG, QXO, CGNX, ALLE, ROAD, GVA) sell off harder than the broad tape despite relief in rates and oil, leaving cyclicals vs. equal-weight S&P back at recent lows. September FOMC minutes showed all participants backing a 25bp hike on insufficient inflation progress, upside inflation risk and balanced labor risk; GS still expects a second hike in December but sees a strong chance further tightening proves unnecessary. Ahead of Friday's DAL print (6% implied move), GS calls positioning mixed (6-7/10): consensus sits below DAL's guide while buyside expects a Q4 acceleration. Separately, GS argues the market is mispricing Corteva (CTVA) post Vylor (VYLR) spinoff - ag chem is a specialty, not commodity, business, and FMC is a poor comp - setting a $20 CTVA target (~38% upside) and initiating VYLR at Buy, $87 target, on moat, licensing and M&A optionality.
